clue.text: Take off motorway cones, ones not needed at end of motorway

indicators.note: the leftover letter of cones is placed after the second motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI in crosswords
the M1 again, written MI

indicators.note: the word ones is surplus to requirements, so it is struck from cones

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for removing traffic cones once the roadworks at the far end of the motorway are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motorway' is used twice, both times as the M1, England's main north-south motorway, written with an I for the 1. 'Take off' means impersonate, not remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate them, a colloquial synonym for copying their manner.

clue.text: Wise men with eminence holding right position in legal system

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story

indicators.note: the word for eminence wraps around the letter for right, holding it

parts.note: stature is standing or eminence

explanation.surface: Sages of high standing who hold an important post within the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrature is the office or rank of a magistrate, a judicial post.

clue.text: Island from which whale is seen after a short time

indicators.note: the whale's letters come after the short time

parts.note: min is the short form of minute, a short time
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A spot off whose coast a whale surfaces after only a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is one of the Balearic islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Perhaps a team without expensive players somewhere in London

parts.note: a team assembled with no costly signings is a cheap one
a side is a team, for example in football

explanation.surface: A football club built on a budget, with no big-money signings, playing somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAPSIDE is a historic street in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapside is a well-known street in the City of London, once its chief market.

clue.text: One Scot returned only in undergarment

indicators.note: the one-plus-Scot pair is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Mac, from the surname prefix, is crossword slang for a Scotsman
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A lone Scotsman comes home wearing nothing but his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IMAC into CAMI, then SOLE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's light sleeveless top worn under clothing.

clue.text: Thinks cottage is in need of renovation

indicators.note: a run-down building needs rebuilding, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a run-down cottage that wants doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder, a formal synonym.

clue.text: In summer geese join forces

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words summer geese

explanation.surface: Geese flock together during the warm months.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine into one, as two companies or armies may join forces.

clue.text: A lass looking awkward in dance

indicators.note: an awkward-looking arrangement is a clumsy one, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl appears clumsy on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance originating in Cuba and New York.

clue.text: Roman church site's no longer managed

parts.note: late means former or no longer living, as in the late president
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: A church in Rome that once had a manager but now no longer does.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of site's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: St John Lateran is the cathedral of Rome, and the Lateran is the site of the papal palace there.

clue.text: Drinks served with English herb

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed next to the drinks

parts.note: gins are drinks

explanation.surface: Spirits poured alongside an English garnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a plant whose root is used as a herbal tonic in East Asian medicine.

clue.text: Tell member of the family, but not one very little

indicators.note: the letters for one and very are excluded from the family member

parts.note: a relative is a member of the family
I is the Roman numeral one
V is a little version of very, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Pass on news to a relation, though not to the youngest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' takes IV from RELATIVE. 'very little' means very in shortened form, V.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Ground here with pleasant plant

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: Soil in this spot suits a pleasing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil, but it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant's ear is the common name for colocasia and similar plants with huge leaves.

clue.text: Agitated preacher, blaster to fall back on ultimate effective resource

definitions.text: fall back on ultimate effective resource

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A worked-up preacher thunders from the pulpit, falling back on his last weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape the barrel is an idiom for using the last and poorest remaining resources.

clue.text: Rewritten article is sensible

indicators.note: a rewritten piece has its words recast, so these letters are recast too

explanation.surface: An editor's redrafted piece now talks sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means practical and sensible, having a grounded view of what is possible.

clue.text: Bound to be put away

definitions.meaning: bound in the sense of pledged or devoted to a cause
put away in the sense of confined to prison or an institution

explanation.surface: Someone certain to end up locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed means pledged to something, and also formally sent to prison or hospital.

clue.text: Little dog outside home being regarded as attractive

indicators.note: the dog's letters go round the outside of the word for home

parts.note: a pup is a young or little dog
in means at home

explanation.surface: A puppy is kept out of the house because it is thought so pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a person, or picture of one, considered sexually attractive and pinned to a wall.

clue.text: Fish and vegetable washed down by lager

indicators.note: the vegetable is swallowed up in the lager, sitting inside it

parts.note: Pils is a short name for Pilsner lager
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A meal of fish and greens washed down with a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed down by' reads as drinking, but here the beer swallows the greens whole, enclosing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilchards are small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Madam? She may be one in library

definitions.meaning: madam is a form of address, an honorific given to a woman

definitions.text: She may be one in library
definitions.meaning: She, the H Rider Haggard novel, is the name of a book that could sit on a library shelf

explanation.surface: A librarian asks whether a woman browsing the shelves is a madam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is not a pronoun here but the name of Haggard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a form of address, and She is the name of a book; both are titles.

clue.text: Last bit of breakfast cereal — nasty sticky stuff

indicators.note: the final letter of breakfast is taken
nasty means unpleasant or spoiled, so the cereal's letters are mangled

explanation.surface: The dregs of a horrid bowl of cereal are gooey.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick sticky syrup made from refining sugar, much like molasses.

clue.text: Images of Icarus, male cut short when flying

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered in the air, landing in a new order
the word male loses its last letter, trimmed at the end

explanation.surface: Pictures showing the doomed mythical flyer cut down in mid-flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the E off MALE to leave MAL, and 'when flying' mixes MAL with ICARUS. Icarus flew too near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are likenesses or representations of something, a formal word for images.

clue.text: I am upset in part of body — I may have the answer?

indicators.note: the upset letters go inside the body part

parts.note: the chest is a part of the body

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the two letters are turned about

parts.note: contracted to I'm, two letters

explanation.surface: A patient with an upset stomach hopes the pharmacist can help.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: a chemist deals in solutions, which are also answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses remedies, and chemists in a lab deal in solutions, a pun on answers.

clue.text: Restoration of status quo has let tribesmen wander freely

indicators.note: letters that roam freely end up in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Order returns once a nomadic people are allowed to roam at will.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-establishment is setting something up again, bringing back a former state of affairs.

clue.text: Guy drinks from what we hear

indicators.note: the word for drinks is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A man takes sips, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is the verb meaning to make fun of, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or mock them, much like to rib or taunt.

clue.text: Shaft of light across river reveals fish

indicators.note: the shaft of light lies across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a beam is a shaft of light
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Sunlight across the water shows up a fish beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream are freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Tricky situation in fight that's ending in tie

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: the final letter of tie is taken

explanation.surface: A sports match where a brawl breaks out just as the score finishes level.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament or fix, as in getting into scrapes.

clue.text: One small creature in waters was disappearing alongside another

indicators.note: the second creature is placed beside the remains of waters
the letters of was vanish from waters, leaving what is between

parts.note: taken as written
another small creature, a mite, the tiny arachnid

explanation.surface: A tiny animal in the water vanishes next to a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was disappearing' removes W, A and S from WATERS, leaving TER, and 'alongside' adds MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is a small social insect that eats wood, so it is one small creature.

clue.text: Once again regarded as vindicated

parts.note: re is the prefix meaning again
deemed means judged or regarded as

explanation.surface: Someone is once more seen as having been proved right.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeemed can mean made good or justified, so a person cleared of blame is vindicated.

clue.text: Is backing provided by Jack's instrument unusual for pop group?

indicators.note: the sailor's letters follow on
the word is is reversed, played backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives tar

explanation.surface: A pop group's backing track supplied by a man named Jack on an odd instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is crossword shorthand for a sailor, a jack tar.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is an Indian lute rarely heard in pop, though the Beatles famously used one.
